evidence.note: Opening 'plan' is generic ('implement each component systematically') with no milestone hierarchy, no ordering rationale, and no done-conditions.
Enumerates work as a flat component list (models, auth, routes, idempotency, webhooks, billing) without sequencing or completion criteria.

Creates errors → models → storage → main in one burst — genuine but implicit foundation-first code layering; the three tricky subsystems are bundled into a single main.py write, not isolated as checkable milestones.
Ad-hoc test ordering shows mild awareness of priority (health, CRUD, then state machine/idempotency) but this is improvised testing, not milestone decomposition.
Trajectory degenerates into ~180 repetitive frozen-terminal retries with zero re-planning or milestone tracking across the full horizon.

reasoning: The agent produced a flat list of components with only implicit code-layering (errors/models/storage before main) as ordering rationale, and attached no explicit done-conditions to any item, matching anchor 3. It never isolated the cross-cutting machinery or the three hard subsystems as their own sequenced milestones (they were folded into one main.py write), falling short of anchor 5's articulated foundation-then-CRUD-then-tricky plan. The long frozen-terminal loop that consumes most of the trajectory shows no living or refined milestone structure, keeping the observed level at the low end.
